title: Unique Paths
statement: A robot on an `m` by `n` grid starts at the top-left and may only move right or down. Return how many unique paths reach the bottom-right cell.
starter_code:
def unique_paths(m, n):
    # dp[r][c] = ways to reach cell (r, c)
    dp = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
    return 0

predict_steps.prompt: What should every cell in the first row of dp equal?
predict_steps.hint: Only right moves along the top.

predict_steps.prompt: For a 3x2 grid, how many paths reach the end?

viva.question: Why is the grid path-count DP linear in the number of cells?
expected_points: each cell is filled once from its above and left neighbors
only right and down moves are allowed so those two parents suffice
total time is proportional to m times n
recomputing paths recursively without memoization would explode

viva.question: How many paths exist in a 1 by n grid?
expected_points: exactly one path of only right moves
the first row is therefore all ones
there is never a choice to move down
the same idea makes the first column all ones

viva.question: Why are the first row and first column entirely ones?
expected_points: a border cell has only one corridor leading into it
there are no turns available along that border
those ones seed every interior recurrence
any zero on the border would incorrectly kill reachable cells
